title: Intent before decoration
summary: Choose visual treatments because they support product intent, hierarchy, interaction, or brand character—not because a treatment is fashionable.
problem: Interfaces become generic when visual decisions are selected from current trends without a clear relationship to user tasks, content, or brand.
use_when: Choosing stylistic direction for a new product
Deciding whether a decorative treatment belongs in a component or page
avoid_when: A platform convention or accessibility requirement already determines the interaction
A decorative experiment is explicitly the product goal rather than a functional interface
rationale: The same visual technique can be excellent in one context and distracting in another.
Design coherence improves when choices can be traced back to product intent.
Agents need explicit rationale to avoid defaulting to fashionable but unrelated patterns.

audit.question: Can each prominent visual treatment be explained by product, interaction, content, accessibility, or brand intent?
